annotation.title_clean: Can Robots go to Heaven? Artificial Intelligence & Moral Standing in Christian Ethics
annotation.title_en: Can Robots go to Heaven? Artificial Intelligence & Moral Standing in Christian Ethics
annotation.venue: University of Chicago, MA Program in the Social Sciences
annotation.summary_en: A University of Chicago MA thesis examining Christian theological and secular (neo-Darwinian, physicalist) views of human intelligence and whether superintelligent AI could merit moral standing. It argues anthropocentrism grounded in discrete human properties is fragile, and the author favours an egalitarian consequentialism without species boundaries.
key_provisions_or_claims: Anthropocentrism based on discrete unique human properties is weaker than holistic or transcendent justifications.
Neo-Darwinian and physicalist views of intelligence allow the possibility of superintelligent AI.
Theological anthropocentrists tend to reject equal moral status for artificial beings.
Physicalist criteria for moral standing could theoretically be met by superintelligent AI.
Historical misplaced anthropocentrism suggests current personhood criteria may be arbitrarily strict.
